parsed.explanation: Structural signals are favourable: no criminalisation of same-sex conduct, no documented trans-specific criminal offence, no documented state targeting, LGBTIQ groups register freely, and an external posture that is protective. The trans-specific record is thin: one undated account of verbal abuse and two physical attacks, with no later incident documented. Tolerance data is LGB-framed and cannot be read as trans acceptance, and the 2010 foreign report records continuing discrimination on gender-identity grounds. The name-change refusal and the labour-code gap are resident-facing and are not scored. Border, facility, custody and care rules are unresolved, which is an open question rather than a known exposure. Extrapolating from the favourable structure with the thin violence record and the unmeasured trans acceptance places this in the reduced-risk band, below the acceptance-with-protections tier.
